canonical_name: LINPACK benchmark, double precision (linpackd) -- Dongarra, Bunch, Moler, Stewart
lineage: LINPACK (1979, Argonne / U New Mexico / Sandia / Michigan): LU factorisation with partial pivoting (DGEFA/DGESL) over the BLAS-1 kernels (DAXPY, DDOT, DSCAL, IDAMAX); the benchmark that defined machine performance for two decades
version: netlib.org/benchmark/linpackd as served 2026-09-12 (file carries its own 'linpack benchmark' revision comments)

source_identity.archive: netlib.org (the authors' own distribution channel since 1985)

license.spdx: public-domain (netlib LINPACK; no licence text in file)

entry_points: PROGRAM (main) in linpackd.f: factor and solve a 100x100 system, report residual and MFLOPS

example.output: norm. resid / resid / machep / x(1) / x(n) lines then the timing table

upstream_docs: Dongarra, Bunch, Moler, Stewart, LINPACK Users' Guide, SIAM 1979

human_capability_summary.built_to: solve dense systems of linear equations Ax=b reliably on the machines of the late 1970s, and (as the benchmark) measure how fast a machine does it
human_capability_summary.pressure: numerical stability under floating-point round-off (partial pivoting), and portability across vendors' Fortran compilers
human_capability_summary.success_means: a small normalised residual on the solved system; for the benchmark, MFLOPS on the 100x100 problem

known_human_problem_solved: dense linear solve with pivoting; the LINPACK MFLOPS number
